tagline.text: A large water park in Biñan beside the SLEX Southwoods exit

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,000 (admission per person; food and lockers extra)

children.text: A 7.5-hectare water park near the SLEX Southwoods exit in southern Metro Manila. With more than 17 attractions, including a steep drop slide and a large wave pool, it is a short drive from Alabang and Muntinlupa and works well as a day trip.

Splash Island is a large water park inside Southwoods City in Biñan, Laguna. It was built with equipment from the Canadian slide designer ProSlide and is described as operated by Global Gutz Parks Phils. Inc. The area is reported at about 7.5 hectares, with more than 17 attractions. Coming down SLEX from central Manila, the Southwoods exit is close by, which makes this one of the first places families and groups think of when they want proper water-park fun near Manila.

The attractions most often mentioned are Magellan's Drop, a near-vertical free-fall slide; Rio Montañosa, a winding tube slide; and Agos Grande, a large wave pool. There are also several other slides, a children's pool, a lazy river (rafting river), food stalls, lockers, a gift shop, and accommodation including glamping. Names and layouts can change with additions and renovations, so check the official information before you go.

Opinions are mixed. Google ratings sit around 4.0 (about 2,800 reviews), and families tend to be happy, with many reviews praising friendly staff and clean showers. On the other hand, some visitors say admission and food are expensive, that time limits on some rides are short, that the nipa huts and slide paint need renovation, and that on some days the pools looked dirty. The common advice is that weekdays are much more relaxed than crowded weekends.

This guide is based on the official site, booking sites, and recent articles, but prices and operating days differ by source. For that reason, prices are given as ranges rather than exact amounts, and you should confirm whether the park is open on your date just before you go. Also, water parks with the same name exist in other countries, so searches can be confusing. In your map app, check for the Southwoods City address in Biñan. It is close to SLEX from southern Manila, so it is popular for weekend day trips, including among Korean families.
A near-vertical free-fall slide, described as the most thrilling ride in the park. There may be height and health restrictions, so check the on-site notices.
A winding tube slide with speed and spins. You carry your tube up many stairs, so expect to use some energy.

A large wave pool at the center of the park. Waves come at set times, so it is best to get in when the waves start. You can feel like you are surfing without going to the sea. Many reviews say it is much less crowded on weekdays.
A course where you lie back on a tube and drift slowly along the current. It is easy for children and older adults, and a good way to rest after the slides.
There are shallow pools and small slides just for smaller children. Access is often decided by height, so check your child's height beforehand.
There are food stalls, lockers (
according to reviews), showers, and a gift shop. Groups and families sometimes rent a shaded hut as a base. Some reviews say lunch is relatively expensive, so it is wise to budget for snacks.
The official site introduces accommodation and "Splash Glamping." It suits those who want to stay a night. You need to inquire about prices and how to book.
The park says it takes company outings, family days, birthday parties, and team-building packages. Corporate rates are by inquiry.

items.title: Full-Day Course
items.subtitle: Enter right at opening and enjoy until the afternoon

children.text: Leave Manila or Alabang and take the SLEX Southwoods exit. Roads can be jammed on weekends, so leaving early is better. Arrive before opening, park, and join the line.
Enter at opening (usually
) and sort out a locker and changing room first. Put valuables in the locker and carry only a waterproof pouch.
In the quiet morning, ride the popular slides such as Magellan's Drop and Rio Montañosa first. Lines grow long by midday.
Eat lunch at the food stalls in the park. Outside food is reported as not allowed, so plan to buy food on site.
Rest on the lazy river, then head to Agos Grande when the waves start. Some attractions may stop admitting people shortly before closing.
Shower, change, and head out. According to reviews, stalls and lockers start closing around 5 PM.
Operating hours and last entry vary by season. One source lists the last ticket redemption as 2 PM.
Let the children get used to the water first at the kids' pool and small slides. Adults rest in nearby shade.
Take a relaxed lap on the lazy river on a tube.
Eat lunch early to avoid the rush.
Play briefly in the wave pool when the waves roll, then gather your things and head back.
After showering, have a snack in the car and leave Manila-bound with time to spare to avoid traffic.
From Makati or BGC, take SLEX south and exit at Southwoods. From Alabang it is described as about
10~15 minutes
by car.
After the exit, follow Southwoods Avenue to the park. In your map app, search for "Splash Island, Southwoods City, Biñan."
Tolls depend on vehicle type and starting point, so confirm on site. One review mentions around ₱150 from Manila or Alabang.
If you drive, you will use the park's parking lot; check parking fees and space on site. For groups, renting a van and going together is convenient.
SLEX is very congested on many weekend mornings. Leave early.
Many people take a bus toward Alabang or FTI, leave SLEX, and get off near the Southwoods exit. Exact stops and routes change over time, so confirm locally.
After getting off, take Grab or a tricycle to the park.
From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), it is around
1~1.5 hours
by Grab or taxi (varies greatly with traffic).
Rather than coming straight from the airport, it is easier to book a night in southern Manila or Alabang first.

The best time for water play is the dry season, December to May. March to May is hot and the water feels refreshing, but you need UV protection. In the rainy season, rain and thunderstorms can stop the slides or change the schedule.

The official site says maintenance days and exclusive-booking days are announced one to two weeks ahead. Some guides say the park opens only Friday to Sunday, while others say daily, so be sure to check. Philippine holidays and school vacations are crowded.

and may vary with local conditions.
The park has food stalls for meals and snacks. Reviews praise the variety of food but also say it is pricey. Outside food and pets are reported as not allowed, so check the rules on site.

For accommodation, you can look into in-park lodging and glamping; cheaper options are hotels in Alabang (Muntinlupa) or central Biñan. For meals, the restaurant floors of the Alabang malls are convenient.

Families with children do well to eat lunch early and set aside a rest period near the lockers. Nearby Southwoods City and Alabang have dining areas, so a common plan is to have dinner after swimming and then head back to Manila.
Lines are much shorter on weekdays. However, check first whether the park is open on weekdays.
You can book online on the official site and on booking sites such as Klook and Traveloka. Prices can be lower than at the gate, so compare.
There is a lot of walking and stairs, so non-slip sandals are comfortable.
Bring a water bottle or tumbler and look for refill points to save on drinks.
Enter early and ride the popular slides first.
Bring sunscreen, a hat, a towel, and a change of clothes. You may not be able to borrow a towel.
Many rides have height limits, so check your child's height before you go.
Put valuables in a locker and carry only a waterproof pouch.
The park may close for rain or maintenance, so check the official site or contact number before leaving. The official site lists contact numbers.
For Korean groups, it helps to tell the park your group size and date in advance when booking. Corporate and group rates must be inquired about.
Prices and operating days differ by source, so be sure to confirm with official information before you visit. The park may be closed on maintenance days.
Slides have height and health restrictions, so follow the lifeguards' instructions.
Pregnant women, people with heart conditions, and those with back or neck problems should avoid the steep drop slides.
Outside food and pets are reported as not allowed.
Some visitor reviews say the pools were not clean on certain days. Be careful if your eyes or skin are sensitive.
On crowded days, never take your eyes off your child and consider using a life jacket.
Promotions such as student and balikbayan (overseas returnee) discounts are sometimes advertised, but conditions change often, so bring ID and proof and confirm locally.
